question: Antidepressant drug that can be used in nocturnal enuresis is?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Imipramine" -> "tricyclic antidepressant" -> "anticholinergic properties" -> "reduces bladder contractions" -> "used in nocturnal enuresis" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Fluvoxamine" -> "SSRI" -> "not primarily indicated for enuresis" -> "less effective for bladder control" -> "not commonly used for nocturnal enuresis" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Phenelzine" -> "MAOI" -> "not indicated for enuresis" -> "primarily used for depression" -> "not effective for bladder control" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Bupropion" -> "atypical antidepressant" -> "not indicated for enuresis" -> "does not have anticholinergic effects" -> "not effective for nocturnal enuresis" -> 65%
analysis: Imipramine is a tricyclic antidepressant that has been used effectively in the treatment of nocturnal enuresis (bedwetting) in children. It works by increasing bladder capacity and reducing the frequency of urination. The other options listed (Fluvoxamine, Phenelzine, and Bupropion) are not typically used for this indication.
